title: Termwise coherent formal equivalence for a closed immersion
statement: theorem closedImmersion_coherentFormal_equivalence_termwise {Z X : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i] [IsNoetherian X] (I : X.IdealSheafData) : ∃ E : @CoherentFormalModule Z (isNoetherian_of_locallyOfFiniteType i) (I.comap i) ≌ ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory (fun M : CoherentFormalModule X I ↦ SupportedOn I M i), Nonempty (E.functor ⋙ ObjectProperty.ι (fun M : CoherentFormalModule X I ↦ SupportedOn I M i) ⋙ ObjectProperty.ι (IsCoherentFormalModule I) ≅ ObjectProperty.ι (IsCoherentFormalModule (I.comap i)) ⋙ (Functor.whiskeringRight ℕᵒᵖ Z.Modules X.Modules).obj (Scheme.Modules.pushforward i))

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Tags 087T, 088A and equation 0880

proof.text: Construct the termwise pushforward lift through coherent formal systems using the proved pushforward-conditions lemma. Its terms are annihilated by the defining ideal: use quasi-coherence and the sectionwise annihilation theorem, translating sectionwise annihilation to zero ideal-module product by tensor sheafification.
Closed pushforward is full and faithful on modules. Mathlib whiskeringRight preserves these properties, and ObjectProperty.lift preserves them, so the restricted system functor is full and faithful.

Apply the existing general exists_formalSystemsPullback theorem. Its equation with the full-subcategory inclusion determines the actual termwise tensor pullback: evaluate the equation on each object and transport the object property. For each supported system these explicit terms have invertible canonical adjunction units by annihilation. Naturality assembles an isomorphism of systems which lifts through both full subcategories, proving essential surjectivity.

Apply Mathlib Functor.asEquivalence to the full, faithful and essentially surjective lift. Its forward functor is this actual lift, so the displayed comparison with termwise pushforward is Iso.refl. No arbitrary equivalence is chosen.
